question: Does any untouched layer in the first X16 archive provide a command-level twin of L0001 strong enough to justify a later image-image synthetic-deletion benchmark without choosing the layer from pixels?

inheritedEvidence.L0001: RC43 established 94,736 nonzero camera-trigger rows and 94,713 AVI frames, but no public per-frame identity key. RC44 and RC45 kept all L0001 pixels sealed.
inheritedEvidence.L0002: RC43 established 95,504 trigger rows and 95,504 AVI frames. RC44 rejected an 8 by 8 command-image bridge and RC45 rejected all 24 documented in-frame-counter interpretations.
inheritedEvidence.archiveIdentity: NIST XYPT_L001-025.zip is 159,164,372 bytes with official SHA-256 7b2b863c843aeabe19f308a5886d57ae241cd386f38c95a7e7ce01e9bc34d007; its sealed central directory contains exactly 25 CSV members.
inheritedEvidence.sidecarSearch: The public X16 record exposes XYPT CSV, AVI, TIFF, layer images, machine records, scan files, and user notes, but no MotionBLITZ .dat/.exp member, camera tick ledger, or trigger-to-frame sidecar has been identified. Absence from the public manifest does not prove that the acquisition laboratory never created one.

inspectedBeforeSeal: Committed RC43-RC45 preregistrations, results, raw-byte receipts, independent audits, and public problem records.
NIST X16 NERDm component names, official archive identity, the already sealed ZIP central-directory metadata, and NIST primary papers on command/measurement/trigger registration.
The complete L0002 XYPT file already used in RC44, without comparing it with any other layer.
Primary research showing that interlayer temperature and scan direction can change melt-pool morphology, so command similarity cannot by itself guarantee image-distribution exchangeability.
notInspectedBeforeSeal: Any L0001 XYPT member row during RC46; prior aggregate counts and member identity are inherited, but the command sequence remains outcome-sealed for candidate selection.
Any L0003-L0025 XYPT member row, trigger-level feature, distance, rank, or pass/fail result.
Any L0001 pixel, compressed AVI member byte, TIFF pixel, natural omission position, or image-derived candidate choice.
Any candidate-layer AVI frame beyond previously published archive directory metadata.

candidateSet.candidates: L0002 through L0025, with no substitution or exclusion after member inspection
candidateSet.dataAllowedForRanking: Only each candidate's complete XYPT command stream and its archive identity. No AVI/TIFF header, pixel, thermal label, defect label, layer image, or build outcome may enter the rank.
candidateSet.triggerRule: Parse every four-column numeric row as X,Y,P,T and retain a camera sample exactly when integer T has bit 1 set, i.e. (T & 2) != 0. Report nonzero-T count separately; disagreement between the two counts stops the run.
candidateSet.malformedRule: A nonempty row with other than four finite numbers, a T value not exactly integral, a member CRC failure, or a parser count disagreement makes the entire comparison inconclusive.

raw: SHA-256 and CRC-32 of every uncompressed XYPT member
total rows, camera-trigger rows, nonzero-T rows, P>0 camera rows, first and last camera tuple

ordinalProfile.construction: Partition camera-trigger rows into 1,024 consecutive equal-ordinal bins using floor(i*1024/N). For each bin compute mean X, mean Y, mean P, fraction P>0, mean step speed to the preceding camera row, and mean unit direction components for nonzero steps.
ordinalProfile.normalization: For each layer center X and Y by its camera-row centroid and divide both by the target L0001 root-mean-square radius. Divide P by the target L0001 maximum positive power and step speed by the target L0001 median positive step speed. No candidate-specific rescaling is allowed.
ordinalProfile.alignment: Fit only a proper 2-D rotation and translation from candidate binned XY means to target binned XY means by orthogonal Procrustes. Reflection, temporal reversal, nonlinear warping, and candidate-specific time shifts are forbidden. Apply the same rotation to direction vectors.

spatialProfile.grid: 32 by 32 fixed cells over the union of target and candidate camera-row X/Y bounds
spatialProfile.channels: All-camera occupancy and P>0-camera occupancy, each normalized to unit mass
spatialProfile.distance: Hellinger distance for each channel after rotating the candidate points with the ordinal-profile rotation; out-of-grid mass is a failure.

segmentProfile.definition: A laser-on segment is a maximal consecutive run of camera-trigger rows with P>0.
segmentProfile.statistics: Segment count; 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th, and 90th percentiles of segment length, within-segment step speed, and positive power; and a 36-bin direction histogram weighted by within-segment path length.
segmentProfile.distance: Absolute relative error for counts and quantiles; Hellinger distance for direction histograms after the fixed proper rotation.

localCorrespondence.construction: Repeat the ordinal aggregation at 4,096 bins and apply the already fitted rotation; do not refit.
localCorrespondence.matchingBin: A bin matches only when center displacement is at most 0.02 target RMS radii, positive-power disagreement is at most 0.05 target maximum power, laser-on fraction differs by at most 0.05, and direction dot product is at least 0.95 whenever both directions are defined.
localCorrespondence.reported: Matching-bin fraction, longest consecutive matching-bin run, and every failed component count.

hardEligibility: Absolute camera-trigger count difference from L0001 is at most 1 percent of 94,736.
P>0 camera-row fraction differs by at most 0.02.
The 1,024-bin Procrustes XY RMSE is at most 0.05 target RMS radii.
The 1,024-bin normalized power RMSE is at most 0.10 and laser-on-fraction RMSE at most 0.05.
Both spatial Hellinger distances are at most 0.10 and segment direction Hellinger distance is at most 0.10.
At least 0.95 of the 4,096 local bins meet every local-correspondence condition.
rankingAndGate.score: For deterministic ranking only, score = count-relative-error + positive-fraction-error + Procrustes-XY-RMSE + power-RMSE + laser-on-RMSE + all-occupancy-Hellinger + on-occupancy-Hellinger + direction-Hellinger + (1-local-match-fraction). Lowest score wins; ties resolve by lower layer number.
rankingAndGate.release: A future image benchmark may use the top-ranked layer only if it passes every hard condition and independent implementations agree on its rank, all metrics to 1e-9, member hashes, and gate. RC46 itself does not acquire candidate AVI pixels.
rankingAndGate.negative: If no candidate passes every hard condition, reject the cross-layer framewise-twin premise for L0001 within layers 2-25. Do not relax thresholds, add transformations, inspect images to rescue a candidate, or describe the closest layer as a valid twin.
rankingAndGate.ambiguity: If more than one layer passes, preserve all passing layers but freeze the lowest-score layer as development and the next-lowest as independent image holdout for the next cycle.

competingHypotheses.claim: No layer in L0002-L0025 is a frame-correspondable command twin of L0001.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Every candidate fails at least one hard eligibility condition.
competingHypotheses.decision: Stop cross-layer pixel acquisition and seek a raw acquisition sidecar or same-layer synthetic control that does not require cross-layer exchangeability.

competingHypotheses.claim: At least one layer repeats L0001 closely enough in command order, geometry, power state, and local direction to justify a prospective image-image deletion benchmark.
competingHypotheses.prediction: At least one candidate passes every hard condition in both implementations.
competingHypotheses.decision: Freeze the top-ranked passing layer and acquire only its authenticated AVI in a later preregistered cycle; passing remains a command-level eligibility result, not proof of equal melt-pool images.

competingHypotheses.claim: A globally similar layer lacks local framewise correspondence.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Aggregate spatial, power, and segment distances are small but the 4,096-bin local-match fraction is below 0.95.
competingHypotheses.decision: Reject it as a deletion-recovery twin even if it is closest by aggregate score.

causalChain: Official, hash-bound XYPT command members and the documented T=2 camera trigger semantics
unknown repetition of scan order across layers plus possible thermal and geometric drift
a candidate preserves target command geometry, power state, direction, and local ordinal correspondence under one proper rotation
two independent parsers agree on a preregistered command-only twin gate
only then may a later independent image benchmark test whether image morphology transfers; natural L0001 remains sealed
fastFailureTests: Check archive SHA-256 and all member CRC-32 values before interpreting metrics.
Stop before ranking on parser disagreement, malformed rows, or T-bit/nonzero-T disagreement.
Evaluate every hard condition independently; the composite score cannot compensate for a failed condition.
Keep command eligibility and thermal/image exchangeability as separate propositions.

independence.implementationA: Node.js standard-library ZIP central-directory, Deflate, CSV, Procrustes, histogram, and gate implementation.
independence.implementationB: Python standard-library zipfile, CSV, linear-algebra, histogram, and gate implementation written without importing Node output.
independence.sharedDependencies: Both consume the same official ZIP and mathematical specification. Agreement detects parsing and implementation faults but not a common conceptual error in the twin definition.
independence.noOutcomeSelection: The candidate rank is sealed from XYPT alone. No image or natural missing-position result is available in RC46.

resourceBudget.prohibited: Do not download AVI/TIFF archives, L0001 AVI member ranges, layer images, or additional X16 archive groups in this cycle. Stream uncompressed CSV members from the ZIP rather than persisting their roughly gigabyte-scale expansion.

uncertaintyBudget.measurement: XYPT stores commanded X,Y,P and trigger state, not encoder position, shutter-open time, interlayer temperature, emissivity, or actual melt-pool state.
uncertaintyBudget.model: Ordinal bins and one proper rotation are a deliberately strict definition of framewise command correspondence; a physically useful nonlinear alignment could exist outside this gate.
uncertaintyBudget.sampling: Only the first 25 of 250 X16 layers are searched; a later layer could be closer, but expanding the candidate set after observing this result requires a new seal.
uncertaintyBudget.implementation: The two implementations share the same archive and preregistered equations; common specification bias remains.
uncertaintyBudget.extrapolation: Passing command similarity does not establish image exchangeability because layer temperature, powder state, optical drift, and accumulated geometry can differ.
uncertaintyBudget.selection: All 24 candidates are enumerated and the score is used only after hard gates, preventing image-driven candidate cherry-picking.

minimumAdvance: A positive result supplies an outcome-blind development/holdout assignment for a later pixel benchmark. A negative result rules out the entire first-25-layer cross-layer shortcut before transferring gigabytes or opening the natural layer.
safetyEthicsEnvironment: Only public NIST machine-command data are read. No hardware is actuated, no personal data are processed, and no defect-certification claim is made. The single 159 MB archive cap bounds network, storage, and computation.
